title: Mechanism of protective function of taurine in neurons and PC 12 cells

sections.abstract: <jats:sec> <jats:label/> <jats:p>Recently, we have shown that taurine could protect cultured neurons from glutamate‐induced neuronal injury by several related mechanisms including inhibiting calcium channels, inhibiting calpain, shifting the ratio of Bcl‐2 and Bax in favor of anti‐apoptosis (J. Neurosci. Res. 87: 1185‐1194, 2009). Furthermore, taurine also exerts protective function against oxidative stress in PC 12 cells. It was found that at 500uM H2O2, the cell viability of PC 12 cells was restored from 20% to more than 80% by taurine at 25 mM. Treatment with taurine restored the H2O2‐induced reduction of expression of Bcl‐2 close to the control level without any significant effect on Bax. In addition, taurine was also found to restore the change of H2O2‐induced alteration of GRP78 and GADD153/CHOP, two marker proteins of ER stress, to the control level suggesting that taurine may also exert protective function against oxidative stress by reducing the ER stress. In summary, taurine appears to exert its protective function against oxidative stress by shifting the ratio of Bcl 2 and Bax in favor of anti‐apoptosis and also protect the integrity of the ER system. In conclusion, taurine exerts its protective function through at least: 1. Lowing the intracellular free calcium level; 2. Inhibiting calpain activity and hence increase the ratio of Bcl‐2/Bax in favor of anti‐apoptosis; 3. Protecting the integrity of ER and mitochondria.</jats:p> </jats:sec>
